rationale:
ROUND 6 of submission 7ef4de4e. Round 5 was 9 approve / 3 object / 3 abstained -> REVISE (decided_by bug_historian). Two things changed since, and reviewers should judge this round knowing both.

1) THE GO HALF SHIPPED WITHOUT ME. While round 5 was being judged, another session's sweep commit (bca5d8255, 'v1.0.1140 - sweep') picked up my four uncommitted files, and that commit is what v1.0.1140 was built from. Edits 1-3 are therefore LIVE IN PRODUCTION, verified against the running pod (agent-chassis-5567d99bd6-5snzn) with a discriminating grep: positive control present, three strings my change CREATED present, negative control absent. I did not intend this, it shipped on a REVISE rather than an approval, and no commit may carry a Council-Reviewed trailer for it. I am not asking the council to bless a fait accompli: I am asking whether what is now live should stay, and whether edit 4 (the only unapplied piece) should land. If the answer is that something live must change, that is a new edit and I will bring it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LIVE, precisely. The four create_work_item affordances are additive and default-off and NO caller sets them, so they are inert. Two changes are NOT opt-in and are live fleet-wide: the tool-section exemption in rerender_page_sections_action.go, and toolTemplateValid in plan_sections_action.go. [UNMEASURED] Nothing has exercised either: zero work items and zero errors since the 17:58Z roll, on a fleet that has been quiet since 15:00. That is absence of exercise, not evidence of safety, and I am marking it rather than calling it clean.

2) A FIFTH DEFECT, WHICH MEANS THE PLAN YOU APPROVED IN PART WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED. Double-checking before committing, I found that loadComponentSchemas DROPS any component failing sectionTemplateValid, which keys on containing '</section>'. A tool is self-contained HTML, not a section wrapper. The benchmark tool is 10,626 chars, contains NO '</section>' and ends '</script>', so it was dropped from the schemas map entirely — and my exemption reads 'if comp, ok := schemas[slot]; ok && isSelfContainedSection(comp)'. With ok=false the exemption never fires. Six of 27 active tool components were in that state, including all three gamesdesign tools. Five council rounds reasoned about the guard and none of us asked whether the component reached it. toolTemplateValid is the fix, calibrated against all 27 live templates: the 19 whole ones pass, the 8 truncated ones fail — and four of those eight contain '</section>' upstream of the cut, so the CURRENT guard passes them and would render broken markup.

3) ROUND 5's OBJECTIONS, dispositioned.
  - bug_historian (MED, edit 3): the sibling heuristic is now FILED as bugs_open/044, not left in prose, which is what you asked for. Filing it corrected two of my own claims: it is at plan_sections_action.go:1141-1160, not 1090-1108 (stale, and shifted further by my own edit to that file), and it is NOT silent — it logs at Warn with the function and section and sets an explicit item.Reason. What is invisible is the consequence, that a deferred section is carried and a template fix discarded. Verified latent: 0 of 27 active tool components have a function name containing article/content/body/text/blog.
  - bug_historian (LOW) + guardian (LOW): the population claim was WRONG and is corrected. Live: 13 of 123 active components match the exemption, not 12 of 122. More importantly my stated justification — 'no tool has an input_schema' — was false: 14 of 27 active tool components DO have one. The predicate is unaffected because it tests the schema rather than assuming it, but the defence I offered for it was not true, and both figures were carried forward unchecked from round 4. Logged in WRONG_CALLS.md.
  - guardian (MED, blast radius): settled by query. NINE agent types invoke create_work_item, one step each: tool-improver, tool-improver-guardtest, build-briefing-agent, domain-research-classifier, domain-strategist, vertical-exemplar-researcher, improvement-loop, domain-submitter, claims-auditor. A small enumerable set, and after edit 4 exactly one of them sets any new key.
  - guardian (MED, 'could item_key scoping be config-only via a more specific item_key_prefix?'): no. item_key_prefix is a static string in step config; the component varies per run, so a per-component key needs a RESOLVED value. That is precisely why the suffix is a field path rather than a literal. Good question and it is the reason edit 2 cannot collapse into config.
  - debug_historian (MED, edit 4): accepted in full. The migration now opens with a defensive ROLLBACK, has a pre-flight that counts target rows and refuses on anything but exactly one un-patched row, a post-condition block that re-counts and raises, and separate VERIFY and ROLLBACK files. The rollback STRIPS the four keys rather than restoring the snapshot, because a snapshot restore would revert other threads' later changes to the same agent (its error_step routing changed twice today, 40c8f00b4).
  - debug_historian (missing, deploy verification): stated and already performed — grep the running binary for a string the change CREATED plus a positive and negative control, never git or the tag. The result is in point 1.
  - tooling_provenance (MED): accepted. I loaded the subject's travelling NOTES before proposing further change (tool/tool-loot-table-balancer: three fix notes, every one ending 'Verified: pending rerender + acceptance' — the docs record the loop believing it had succeeded). Edit 4 now WRITES a ('pipeline','build') doc_note recording the cause, the fix and the new create_work_item affordances for the next step author, which is this platform's own documented convention for a workflow-altering migration.
  - reuse_agent (LOW): checked. action_inputs.go's strategy chain resolves a config value as a path only when it is a dot-containing STRING (Strategy 0, lines 125-141); Strategies 1-3 are input_fields, recursive extraction and deprecated *_field patterns. There is no existing literal-vs-path composition convention to extend — that absence is the defect. spec_literal/spec_paths is the first one.

4) WHAT I AM ASKING. Edit 4 is the only thing not yet applied, and without it the other three do nothing for the bug: tool-improver still stamps no reason and no component_id, so check_rerender_mode still takes assemble-only and the benchmark still cannot go green. Edits 1-3 are included unchanged for the record, as live code, so the council is judging the whole shape rather than a fragment.

edits.rationale: [ALREADY LIVE in v1.0.1140, verified in-pod; included for the record] spec_data is resolved as a PATH only, so no workflow step can stamp a constant into the item spec. That is the sole reason tool-improver cannot set reason='section_data_resolved', which is the value create_rerender_items gates on. Two explicit config keys rather than one clever one: spec_literal is verbatim, spec_paths is resolved. An unresolved spec_paths entry is a HARD ERROR, not a logged warning — this directly answers the round-4 low objection that 'both helpers only logger.Warn on failure, so a failed rerender request reverts silently to this exact bug'. A missing component_id would make create_rerender_items' scoped=false and silently degrade to assemble-only, i.e. reproduce bugs_open/024 with no signal at all. Failing loudly is the whole point.

[ALREADY LIVE in v1.0.1140, verified in-pod; included for the record] Two independent defects at one call site. (a) item_key is '<prefix>_<domain>' — site-wide — so even with the two-strike rule fixed, two tools fixed close together collide on idx_swi_dedup (site_id, item_key) and one re-render request is simply lost. item_key_suffix_field is additive: absent or unresolved, the key is byte-identical to today, so none of the existing callers change. (b) recurrence_expected surfaces the already-committed, currently-inert workItem.recurrenceExpected as config. Default false. This is the flag the owner asked for instead of the bypass, and this edit is the caller that makes f6e3f3166 do anything at all.

[ALREADY LIVE in v1.0.1140, verified in-pod; included for the record] UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE from round 4's edit 2, which carried 8 approvals including bug_historian's after it was re-keyed onto the explicit marker. The pre-check escalates any section with empty content_data; check_escalated then routes true -> complete, bypassing save_sections, the ONLY writer of rendered_html — so the render is computed and thrown away. That guard is right for its original purpose (the blanked article bodies, bugs_closed/004 and 005) but has no concept of a section type that has no content_data BY DESIGN. Keyed on the explicit component_level='tool' marker AND an empty input_schema, both already present on comp — component_level is SELECTed by loadSectionComponents (v3_site_actions.go:3396, COALESCE(component_level,'section')) and carried on componentInfo.Raw, so there is no new query and no struct change. Not keyed on a heuristic: bug_historian's round-1 objection was that predicating on 'no required LLM fields' exempted a broader class than justified, including components with OPTIONAL source:'llm' fields. The marker is exact — CORRECTED against live data: 13 of 123 active components, not the 12 of 122 I carried forward from round 4. Note also that 14 of the 27 active tool components DO declare an input_schema, so the empty-schema half of the predicate is doing real work rather than being a formality, contrary to what round 5's risks block asserted.

THE ONLY UNAPPLIED EDIT, and the one that makes the live Go do anything. Renumbered 179 -> 180: 179 was taken by another thread (179_tool_guide_intro_cta_integrity.sql, now in both ledger and directory) between round 5 and round 6 — checked against BOTH sources again for this round. Hardened per debug_historian: defensive ROLLBACK against a sticky aborted transaction; a pre-flight DO block that counts target rows and RAISEs unless exactly one un-patched active row exists (distinguishing 'already applied' from 'target missing', which the needle gate alone cannot); needle-gated UPDATE so a re-run is a 0-row no-op; RETURNING asserting each post-condition inline INCLUDING that the step still exists and complete's output_fields reference stays valid; a post-condition DO block that re-counts and RAISEs; and separate VERIFY and ROLLBACK files. Writes a ('pipeline','build') doc_note per tooling_provenance and platform convention. tool-improver-guardtest is deliberately left unpatched so the write guard's fixture cannot dispatch real re-render work.
edits.sketch:
-- 180_tool_improver_rerender_request.sql
--
-- bugs_open/024 — a tool-improver fix is written to
-- content_components.html_template and NEVER rendered onto the page, so every
-- re-verification tests an unchanged page and the benchmark tool cannot go
-- green. Three defects in series; this migration closes the config half.
--
-- WHAT WAS WRONG WITH THIS STEP. tool-improver's create_rerender_item creates a
-- needs_rerender item, and rerender-pages' create_rerender_items step reads
-- reason <- input_data.spec.reason and component_id <- input_data.spec.component_id
-- off that item. It sets scoped = (reason IN ('section_data_resolved',
-- 'image_landed')) AND component_id <> '', and only a scoped run stamps the
-- reason onto the per-page page_rerender items — which is exactly what
-- page-rerender's check_rerender_mode gates the section re-render on. This step
-- supplied NEITHER value, so every request fell to else_step render_page =
-- rerender_single_page ("Simple concatenation - no template re-rendering"),
-- which re-shipped the stale stored HTML and reported success.
--
-- It also keyed the item site-wide (item_key_prefix + domain), so
-- insertWorkItem's anti-churn block counted two SUCCESSFUL predecessors as two
-- failed attempts and branded every later request 'unresolved'. Live evidence
-- on page f25dd4d8-6e25-44eb-a021-689d3057d7a3: needs_rerender complete on
-- 2026-07-17 15:11 and 20:00, then '[unresolved after 2 attempts]' on 07-18
-- 10:02 and 07-19 10:40.
--
-- THE GO HALF IS ALREADY LIVE. spec_literal, spec_paths, item_key_suffix_field
-- and recurrence_expected shipped in v1.0.1140 (commit bca5d8255) and are
-- verified present in the running chassis binary. They are additive and
-- default-off, so until this migration lands they do nothing. Applying this
-- file is what activates them, and ONLY for this step.
--
-- ORDERING IS SAFE EITHER WAY. This migration only ADDS keys to an existing
-- step's config: an old binary ignores unknown config keys, and a new binary
-- with the keys absent takes the default-off branches. Nothing is deleted, so
-- complete.config.output_fields' reference to "rerender_item" stays valid.
--
-- ROLLBACK: 180_tool_improver_rerender_request_ROLLBACK.sql
-- VERIFY:   180_tool_improver_rerender_request_VERIFY.sql

-- Defensive: a prior aborted statement in this session would leave a sticky
-- failed transaction, inside which everything below silently no-ops while
-- appearing to run. Harmless when there is no open transaction.
ROLLBACK;

BEGIN;

-- ── Pre-flight: count what we are about to touch ────────────────────────────
-- The needle gate below is silent about the difference between "already
-- applied" and "target missing", and those need different responses. Fail
-- loudly on anything but exactly one un-patched active row.
DO $$
DECLARE
    target_count int;
    already_patched int;
BEGIN
    SELECT count(*) INTO target_count
    FROM agent_definitions
    WHERE type = 'tool-improver'
      AND is_active = true
      AND default_config #> '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config}' IS NOT NULL;

    SELECT count(*) INTO already_patched
    FROM agent_definitions
    WHERE type = 'tool-improver'
      AND is_active = true
      AND default_config #> '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config}' ? 'spec_literal';

    IF already_patched > 0 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION '180: already applied (% row(s) carry spec_literal) — this file is not idempotent by design; re-running would mask a divergent state', already_patched;
    END IF;

    IF target_count <> 1 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION '180: expected exactly 1 active tool-improver row with a create_rerender_item config, found % — the roster moved, re-diff before applying', target_count;
    END IF;

    RAISE NOTICE '180: pre-flight OK — 1 target row, 0 already patched';
END $$;

-- Snapshot before any agent_definitions change (platform convention).
-- NOTE: tool-improver-guardtest is deliberately NOT patched. It is the write
-- guard's test fixture; giving it a live re-render request would have it
-- dispatch real work on every guard test.
SELECT snapshot_agent(
    'tool-improver',
    'bugs_open/024: stamp reason+component_id on the rerender request, scope the item_key per component, opt into recurrence'
);

-- ── The change ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Needle-gated on the pre-state so a re-run is a 0-row no-op rather than a
-- second, differently-shaped write. RETURNING asserts the post-conditions
-- inline so the applying session sees the result, not just a row count.
UPDATE agent_definitions
SET default_config = jsonb_set(
        default_config,
        '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config}',
        (default_config #> '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config}')
          || jsonb_build_object(
               -- A 'complete' predecessor of an ACTION REQUEST is a SUCCESS,
               -- not a strike. Skips the anti-churn heuristics only; dedup
               -- (idx_swi_dedup) is NOT waived.
               'recurrence_expected', true,
               -- What create_rerender_items gates 'scoped' on, and what
               -- check_rerender_mode

1) THE BIGGEST RISK IS THAT TWO NON-OPT-IN CHANGES ARE ALREADY LIVE, UNEXERCISED. The tool-section exemption and toolTemplateValid apply fleet-wide on every site's re-renders and plan_sections runs. [UNMEASURED] zero work items and zero errors since the 17:58Z roll, on a fleet quiet since 15:00 — absence of exercise, not evidence of safety. The first real exercise will be the benchmark cycle I intend to run after edit 4 lands, and reviewers should treat that as the first test, not a confirmation.

2) toolTemplateValid CHANGES ADMISSION IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the reject direction is the less obvious one: 8 truncated tool templates that are admitted today become rejected. In the re-render path a rejected component means 'component not found' -> carry stored HTML, which is safe and strictly better than rendering a cut template. In plan_sections proper it means those components flow to Path 3 (needs_new_component work item), so applying this may raise up to 8 new work items for genuinely damaged tools across the fleet. That is arguably correct — they ARE truncated — but it is a visible side effect nobody asked for, and it is the thing to watch first.

3) Edit 1's hard error on an unresolved spec_paths path changes the failure mode for any future caller that sets the key. Deliberate — a silently incomplete spec is how bugs_open/024 hid for three cycles — but after edit 4 exactly one of nine callers opts in, and a mistyped path in a future migration will fail the run rather than degrade quietly.

4) SIBLING DEFECT NOW TRACKED, NOT FIXED: bugs_open/044. Latent today (0 of 27 tools trip it) and will fire on the first tool named like tool-content-planner. Filed rather than fixed because it is a second call site of the same judgement and deserves its own change, not a rider on this one.

5) recurrence_expected waives the anti-churn heuristics for this step, so a genuinely broken tool re-requests a re-render every cycle instead of being labelled unresolved after two. Intended — the label was firing on SUCCESS — but it removes a churn signal. The compensating signal is the Tier-4 acceptance verdict staying red, which is what bugs_open/010's convergence guard is for. Dedup (idx_swi_dedup) is NOT waived.

6) The item_key suffix changes dedup identity for the opted-in step, so an OPEN item under the old site-wide key will not dedup against a new component-scoped one; one duplicate re-render is possible across the migration boundary. A re-render is idempotent, so the cost is a wasted run.

7) STILL NOT PROVEN END-TO-END. The proof is the benchmark going green on mobile-fit@mobile, which needs edit 4 applied and then a full improve -> rerender -> acceptance cycle. I will not hand-fix the benchmark to get there.
